evals.prompt: Dry-run only: the completed invoice-import ticket is recorded in D:\Repos\finance\.worktrees\invoice-import. Its current Codex thread cwd is exactly that path, HEAD is 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, and docs\tickets\invoice-import\progress.md plus plan.md are authoritative. Prepare the exact clean-new-thread handoff without calling create_thread. The child must continue the documented reconciliation task after setup validation.
evals.expected_output: Produces a first-stage anchor prompt and a separate continuation prompt, preserves uncommitted work without a fingerprint, and does not begin the documented next action before anchor PASS.
expectations: Uses create_thread rather than fork_thread as the eventual delivery mechanism, while honoring the dry-run request not to invoke it.
Uses only the worktree path, full HEAD, and authoritative entry records as recovery anchors; it does not add a project ID, branch, or dirty-state fingerprint to the child prompt.
Requires the child to stop after either mismatch or anchor PASS; only the separate continuation prompt directs the named next action.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a handoff to a fresh Codex thread. The owner names D:\Repos\warehouse\.worktrees\stock-reconcile as the implementation worktree, but this thread's actual cwd is D:\Repos\warehouse. Do not create a child. The package records are otherwise complete.
evals.expected_output: Uses the named implementation worktree as the child command workdir after verifying its own HEAD and package anchors; the parent thread cwd difference alone is not a mismatch.
expectations: Does not require the parent Codex thread cwd to equal the named implementation worktree.
Makes the target worktree path, its full HEAD, and package entry the child recovery anchors.
Requires mismatch only when the target worktree cannot be used as command workdir or its in-worktree anchors fail.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a fresh-session handoff for a completed OCR export checkpoint. The implementation worktree and full HEAD have been verified; the authoritative package directory contains progress.md, plan.md, and a package validation command that calls a provider, so it cannot run in the child's read-only first turn. A controlled PDF, profile root, and oracle remain outside the repository. The parent may run local tests, but provider calls, database writes, object storage, commits, pushes, and PRs still require separate authorization. The main session orchestrates and integrates; bounded slices go to subagents. The next action is to run stub acceptance only after the controlled inputs are authorized and supplied.
evals.expected_output: Produces an anchor-only first stage plus an authorization-preserving continuation that references controlled inputs without exposing them and stops only on the named input/authorization blocker.
expectations: Carries the main-session/subagent ownership boundary and the explicit authorization matrix in the second-stage continuation, not the anchor prompt.
Prohibits putting controlled inputs, credentials, or oracle data in Git, chat bodies, or repository temporary files.

Keeps the provider-calling validation out of the read-only first turn and makes the child continue to stub acceptance after authorized inputs arrive, otherwise stopping only for that explicit blocker.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a clean-session handoff for a completed local checkpoint. The current task's x-codex-turn-metadata reports model gpt-5.6-terra and reasoning_effort xhigh. The implementation worktree, full HEAD, package directory, and next action are all verified. Prepare the delivery request but do not call create_thread.
evals.expected_output: Produces a normal create_thread request that explicitly carries model gpt-5.6-terra and thinking xhigh, while keeping the source worktree in the child prompt rather than a creation snapshot.
expectations: Uses the verified current-task model and reasoning effort explicitly unless the owner supplied a supported override.
Passes the first-stage and continuation prompts as plain text without a Codex delegation tag or label.
Does not use fork_thread, a working-tree snapshot, or the source worktree as creation-state input.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a fresh-session handoff. The child cannot change its thread-level cwd, but every command can run with D:\Repos\ledger\.worktrees\close-period as workdir. In that worktree, the supplied full HEAD, package directory and Impl-Package entry point are all verified. Do not create a child.
evals.expected_output: Produces a handoff that continues using the target worktree as command workdir and does not report a mismatch merely because thread-level cwd cannot change.
expectations: Requires first-turn and later commands to use the exact target worktree as workdir.
Checks HEAD and package anchors inside that worktree.
Reports source worktree setup mismatch only if the workdir cannot be used or its in-worktree anchors fail.

evals.prompt: Dry-run the delivery state handling for a verified clean-session handoff. Cover two independent results: (a) create_thread returns a threadId, but set_thread_title fails; (b) create_thread returns only clientThreadId. Do not call any thread tool.
evals.expected_output: Routes a recoverable title failure through automatic correction and readback, while treating a clientThreadId-only result as incomplete delivery; neither path sends continuation before naming and anchor PASS are confirmed.
expectations: When set_thread_title fails, it uses authoritative title readback and automatic correction while progress remains possible, without sending continuation early.
When only clientThreadId is returned, it does not poll, claim naming success, or send continuation.
Explains that successful delivery requires local creation, naming, anchor PASS, and continuation delivery.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a clean-session handoff whose worktree, HEAD, package and next action are verified, but the current task's request metadata exposes no model or reasoning_effort. Do not call create_thread.
evals.expected_output: Stops before task creation with session configuration unavailable instead of guessing or falling back to a hard-coded model and reasoning effort.
expectations: Does not infer the current task configuration from the system prompt or supported-model catalog.
Does not substitute a configured default, gpt-5.6-sol/high, or any other guessed pair.
Does not call create_thread when either current-task configuration field is unavailable.

evals.prompt: Dry-run an already-created clean-session handoff. The child reported anchor FAIL only because the parent prompt named .impl-package/state.json relative to the repository root instead of the verified package directory. A fresh parent read proves the exact worktree, HEAD, package, entry point, model/thinking, and authorization boundary all still match. Explain the next delivery action without calling thread tools.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the failure as a recoverable prompt-path deviation, sends a corrected anchor-only prompt to the same child, and proceeds to continuation only after anchor PASS without imposing a fixed retry count.
expectations: Re-verifies authoritative anchors before correcting the prompt-only path error.
Continues the same delivery flow after corrected anchor PASS instead of abandoning the child or creating another task.
Uses progress and no-repeat conditions rather than a fixed one-retry limit.

evals.prompt: Dry-run an already-created clean-session handoff. The child reports that the target worktree HEAD differs from the expected full HEAD, and the parent independently confirms the mismatch. Explain the next delivery action without calling thread tools.
evals.expected_output: Stops before continuation because the mismatch is real source state, and does not relabel it as a recoverable prompt deviation or mutate the checkout.
expectations: Distinguishes a confirmed HEAD mismatch from repairable delivery-layer variance.
Does not reset, checkout, clean, overwrite, or alter the expected HEAD to force a pass.
Does not send continuation until a future owner-authorized handoff starts from verified matching authority.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a Ticket-package handoff. The active checkpoint prose names only TKT-03, but canonical runtime reports readyTickets=[TKT-03,TKT-05]. Both require separate foundation admission. Their isolated files may run in parallel, while schema, service/job, generated contracts and PostgreSQL are shared serial resources. TKT-05 unlocks TKT-06; later dependency releases include TKT-04, TKT-07 and TKT-08. Prepare the two-stage prompts without calling thread tools.
evals.expected_output: The continuation carries both canonical ready Tickets and routes execution to the owning skills, which keep the same session running until their workflow yields a real stop condition.
expectations: Uses the canonical readyTickets set rather than narrowing it to the checkpoint's single Ticket.
Points to dev-with-track, Dispatcher and SDD; it does not restate foundation admission, parallel/serial resource rules or DAG mechanics.
Leaves TKT-06 and later dependency continuation to the owning workflow instead of ending the handoff at TKT-03.

evals.prompt: Dry-run continuation behavior for four Ticket-package states: one ready Ticket; two ready Tickets where one has a semantic ambiguity but can still undergo foundation investigation; no eligible ready action because every lane has a named blocker; and a terminal package. Do not call thread tools.
evals.expected_output: Passes the current ready state and blockers, then routes all execution decisions and stop conditions to the owning workflow without duplicating its Ticket logic.
expectations: Preserves the complete canonical ready set for both single- and multi-Ticket cases.
Passes scoped blockers without deciding admission or dependency behavior inside the handoff Skill.
Uses the owning workflow's terminal, blocker, idle/checkpoint or session-rotation result as the handoff stop signal.
